ig_carousel_topic.topic: Why your win rate matters less than your ROI
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
You can win 60% of your bets and still lose money.
You can win 52% and be profitable.
Win rate alone tells you almost nothing.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Most bettors fixate on win rate.
It feels like the scoreboard. Win more than you lose, you're ahead.
But it ignores the most important variable: the odds on every bet.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
ROI measures how much you return per unit risked, across all bets.
A 54% win rate at -110 average odds produces roughly 3% ROI.
A 52% win rate at +120 average odds produces roughly 6% ROI.
The second bettor wins less often and makes more money.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Real example from our 2026 track record:
243-204, 54.4% win rate.
Net +37.7u on 447 bets. ROI: 9.3%.
If every bet had been -110, that win rate would yield about 3.5u. Line shopping and edge selection account for the rest.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
Win rate is a partial picture. ROI is the full one.
If you're not tracking units won and average odds, you're missing the number that actually matters.
SmarterPicks posts both. Every day, every bet.
